#                                      CDF form and the data have undergone calibration and decompression from the                           
#                                      binary MSL RAD EDR data.                                                                              
#     DESCRIPTION                     This file contains data from RAD_RDR: Radiation Assessment Detector on the Mars                       
#                                      Science Laboratory (MSL). There is one sols worth of observations where each                          
#                                      observation can have four types of data: (1) Counters, (2) Histograms, (3)                            
#                                      Dosimetry, and (4) PHA data. These data are organized in a hierarchical fashion                       
#                                      in which some observations may not have all four types. These are described                           
#                                      in the data object sections. For additional information and details concerning                        
#                                      data organization, science meaning, etc., please refer to the Data Set Catalog,                       
#                                      MSLRAD_RDR_DS.CAT.1                                                                                   
#     QUALITY_FLAG_NOTE               Dataset contains all data, however data is flagged (FLAGGED_DATA) if there are                        
#                                      quality issues(cmds > 2, DAN firing, data corruption, &c.                                             
#     DURATION_NOTE                   A RAD instrument observation is the 'sampling period', for each observation                           
#                                      there are variables DURATION and ALIVE_TIME that both are indicators of the                           
#                                      length of the observation.  Though similar, they have slightly different meanings,                    
#                                      the DURATION (a coarse timer with 1 sec res) is the period from when RAD began                        
#                                      acquiring data, until RAD stopped taking data.  The ALIVE_TIME (10us res) is                          
#                                      based on how many seconds the hardware was able to accept incoming particles.                         
#                                      ALIVE_TIME has a companion variable DEAD_TIME, which indicates how many seconds                       
#                                      the hardware was 'busy' processing (and hence cannot accept an incoming particle).                    
#                                       In most nominal cases, the most accurate what to determine the observations                          
#                                      active period is ALIVE_TIME + DEAD_TIME.   There can be exceptions, if the                            
#                                      ALIVE_TIME counter maxxed out.  In those cases the DURATION would be used.                            
#     PI_AFFILIATION                  SwRI-Boulder

#     SOURCE_NAME                     MSL
#     TEXT                            The Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD) and its data products are described                           
#                                      in detail in the literature (Hassler et al., 2012). Each RAD observation contains                     
#                                      the following: (1) Instrument counters, (2) Neutral particle count histograms                         
#                                      in detectors D and E, (3) LET count histograms, (4) Absorbed dose rate in detectors                   
#                                      B and E, (5) High-cadence dose rate in B and E (16 rates per observation).
